role: ArchiveStore's persistence mechanics: the locked write path (_archive with tombstone/schema gates, rrSeries splice, same-night merge, atomic write + index save with rollback), the hash-checked read path, dual-format (encrypted/legacy) decoding, split-night segment normalisation, tombstones + deletion times, and batch archiving.
types: ArchiveStore: extension — internal write/read/delete/batch mechanics over SessionArchive state
ArchiveStore.StoredRRSeries: enum — preserved(beats, viaRawDecode)/noBeatsStored/unreadable outcome of reading stored beats
ArchiveStore.OverlapVerdict: enum (private) — keepLonger/distinct for segment dedupe
ArchiveStore.BatchOutcome: struct (private) — newEntries + updatedIds of one archiveBatch pass
state: static ArchiveStore.minMeaningfulSegment = 600 s (segments shorter are dropped as artifacts)
ud:archive.deletionTimes (standard suite; [uuidString: epoch seconds] dictionary, ArchiveStore.deletionTimesKey)
toplevel: File-scope private func verifyHash (fileprivate). No global state besides the static constants and the deletion-times queue/key above. Header comment states underscored/private helpers assume the caller holds archive.archiveLock while exists/delete/archiveBatch/entries etc. take it themselves.

units.does: Locked-caller write entry: runs guardWritable (tombstone + newer-schema gates), splices stored rrSeries onto a beat-less incoming session, then either folds an overnight into a same-night/copy target (sameNightMerge) or writes file + index (writeAndIndex); returns the resulting index entry.

branches.cond: sameNightMerge returned an entry (session was folded into an existing archived session)
branches.effect: return that entry (keyed by the OLDER session's id); otherwise fall through to writeAndIndex

units.does: Throws sessionWasDeleted when the session id is tombstoned, or newerSchemaVersion(v) when the session was decoded from a schema newer than HRVSession.currentSchemaVersion; otherwise returns.

branches.effect: log + throw ArchiveError.sessionWasDeleted (blocks CloudKit-race resurrection); else continue
log warning + throw newerSchemaVersion(v); else return normally (nil version = legacy, allowed)

units.does: If the incoming session has rrSeries == nil and the id is already indexed, reads the stored copy's beats (storedRRSeries) and splices them back onto the session before it is written; returns the (possibly patched) session.

branches.cond: session.rrSeries == nil AND archive.index contains this id
branches.effect: continue to splice; otherwise return session unchanged (has beats or is new)
break silently; when true log a warning that the raw reader salvaged the beats and the re-archive heals the hash
nothing to splice (file read fine, no beats)
log .error and return the session WITHOUT beats, so the following write overwrites the stored file's rrSeries

flags.text: On .unreadable the re-archive proceeds and overwrites the stored file with rrSeries=nil. Unreadable includes a decrypt failure while the encryption key is unavailable (plaintextBytes/loadAndDecodeSessionFile both call encryptionManager.decrypt); writeAndIndex only aborts when the raw bytes cannot be read, not when they cannot be decrypted, so a lightweight-loaded session re-archived while the key is unreachable replaces a night's intact encrypted beats with a beat-less plaintext file. The log text claims the data 'was already unrecoverable on disk', which is false for a transient decrypt failure.

units.does: Reads the stored session for id: via hash-checked _retrieve first; on failure via the hash-agnostic loadAndDecodeSessionFile on the indexed file. Returns preserved(beats, viaRawDecode), noBeatsStored, or unreadable.

branches.effect: return .preserved(rrSeries, viaRawDecode:false) or .noBeatsStored when its rrSeries is nil; errors are discarded by try? and fall to the raw path

branches.cond: an index entry exists AND the raw decode succeeded
branches.effect: continue; otherwise (no entry, or decode/decrypt threw — error discarded) return .unreadable

units.does: For a NEW overnight (not a re-archive, merge not skipped, no explicit linkedSessionIds) with a same-sleep gap configured, finds a merge target; if found, loads it, merges the incoming session's data into it (SessionMerger) and re-archives the existing session, discarding the new UUID. Returns the merged entry, or nil to write standalone; rethrows a retrieve/archive failure.

branches.effect: hasExplicitLinks true → guard fails → return nil

branches.cond: not a re-archive, not skipped, sessionType == .overnight, no explicit links, sameSleepGap non-nil (merge mode not .off), mergeTarget found
branches.effect: proceed to merge; any failing condition returns nil (caller writes standalone)

branches.cond: existing.recoveryScore nil / session.recoveryScore nil (?? "nil" in log)

branches.effect: return nil → caller writes the new session standalone (a same-night duplicate); non-nil merges and re-archives existing
log warning and rethrow so the caller does not mark the backup archived

flags.text: The doc above says a retrieve failure must not fall through to the standalone write, but a nil from _retrieve (entryById miss, possible only through a stale sessionIdLookup cache) does exactly that via `else { return nil }`.

The doc says a NEW overnight that is a copy of an archived recording merges into it, but the guard requires sameSleepGap(for:) to be non-nil, which is nil when sessionMergeMode == .off; with merging off an overlapping copy with a different UUID is written standalone by _archive, while archiveBatch (archiveOne) merges the same copy because it calls mergeTarget with a nil gap. MergeTarget's own comment says with merging off 'only copies of the same recording merge'.

units.does: Encodes the session (encrypted when possible) to <uuid>.json with format-dependent protection options, replaces/appends its index entry and saves the index; on save failure restores the previous index and file and rethrows. Reads the previous file bytes first (throws if they cannot be read).

branches.cond: a file already existed at the path
branches.effect: read its bytes (throws → whole write aborted before anything is written); else previousData = nil
rollBackWrite (restore index, caches, previous file or remove new file) then rethrow; on success return the new entry

units.does: Encodes the session with SessionArchive.sessionEncoder (compact sortedKeys) via SessionFileCodec.encodeForDisk and returns (bytes, sha256 of bytes-as-written, write options for the resulting format, which also records/clears the PendingEncryptionLedger entry).

After a failed index save: restores archive.index to the pre-write snapshot, nils sortedEntriesCache and sessionIdLookup, and either rewrites the previous file bytes or removes the newly created file; file-rollback failures are only logged via attempt().

branches.cond: previousData is non-nil (file existed and was read)
branches.effect: rewrite it with [.atomic, .completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication] inside attempt (error logged, swallowed)

branches.cond: no previous data AND file did not exist before
branches.effect: remove the new file inside attempt (error logged, swallowed); if it existed but previousData is nil nothing is restored (cannot happen: writeAndIndex throws before writing in that case)

flags.text: The rollback rewrites the previous bytes with .completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication whatever they were, and the failed write's archiveWriteOptions has already cleared (encrypted case) the PendingEncryptionLedger entry; if the previous file was plaintext pending encryption it is restored with the weaker protection class and no longer queued for re-encryption.

units.does: Locked-caller hash-checked read: looks up the entry, reads bytes, verifies SHA256 against entry.fileHash, decrypts/passes through to plaintext, and decodes HRVSession with the full sessionDecoder (rrSeries included). Returns nil when the id is not indexed.
Resolves the entry's file URL (relative or legacy absolute) and returns its bytes; throws fileNotFound if absent, rethrows read errors (e.g. EPERM).

Turns stored bytes into plaintext JSON: 'FR'-prefixed bytes are decrypted (errors rethrown); JSON-looking bytes pass through; anything else is decrypt-attempted with failure falling back to the raw bytes.

branches.cond: catch: decrypt of FR bytes threw
decrypt of non-JSON, non-FR bytes fails (?? fallback)
branches.effect: return the raw bytes (decoder then reports dataCorrupted); success returns decrypted legacy Format 2/3 plaintext

units.does: True when data has >=2 bytes starting 0x46 0x52 ('FR' magic of current EncryptionManager format).
Scans up to the first 8 bytes skipping whitespace/BOM-first-byte; true if the first significant byte is '{' or '['; false otherwise or if only whitespace in the first 8 bytes.

branches.cond: for each of the first 8 bytes
branches.effect: iterate; falling off the end returns false

units.does: Reads a session file at a URL and decodes it with the given decoder, handling FR-encrypted (decrypt, errors thrown), plaintext JSON, and legacy Format 2/3 ciphertext (decrypt attempted, failure falls back to raw bytes). No hash check.

branches.effect: swallow; decode raw bytes so JSONDecoder throws dataCorrupted

units.does: For a session with linkedSessionIds, loads each linked session's span, normalises all segments (own + linked) for split-night display, and returns only the linked ones (excluding the current id), or nil when there are none.

branches.effect: current end = startDate → normalizer returns [] (end not after start) → result nil

units.does: Loads one linked session via archive.retrieve (full, hash-checked, takes lock) and returns its (id,start,end) segment; nil when missing, zero/negative length, or the read throws (logged).

branches.effect: end = start → next guard returns nil
return nil; else return the segment
log warning and return nil (segment silently missing from display)

units.does: Pure: computes the current session's own stretch, merges it with linked segments, drops segments <10 min, sorts by start, collapses duplicate/contained ranges and merges ranges separated by < SleepConstants.defaultSplitGapMinutes.

Pure: derives the current session's unique segment — after the latest linked end (child case), before the earliest linked start (parent case), or its own bounds — and returns nil when shorter than 10 minutes.

branches.cond: max linked end exists and lies strictly inside (start, end)
else min linked start exists and is after start

units.does: Pure: walks start-sorted segments, keeping the longer of any pair judged the same segment (overlapVerdict) and appending distinct ones.
Replaces the last kept segment with the candidate when the candidate is strictly longer.

branches.effect: return without change; else replace last

units.does: Pure: .keepLonger when starts and ends are both within 5 min, when the pair overlaps >= duplicateContainmentRatio (0.85) of the shorter, or when either is contained in the other within 5 min tolerance; else .distinct.

branches.cond: either range contained in the other (±5 min)

units.does: Pure: true when the overlap of two segments is >= 0.85 of the shorter one's duration.
Pure: segment end minus start in seconds.
Pure: merges consecutive segments whose gap is shorter than SleepConstants.defaultSplitGapMinutes*60, extending the earlier segment's end (keeps the earlier id).

branches.cond: gap from last end >= continuity threshold
branches.effect: append as a separate segment; else extend last.end to max(last.end, segment.end)

units.does: O(1) id→entry lookup using the cached sessionIdLookup dictionary, building and caching it from archive.index (last duplicate wins) on a cache miss. Caller holds the lock.

branches.effect: return lookup[id]; else build, store and return

units.does: Takes the lock and returns all index entries sorted newest-first by date, using/filling sortedEntriesCache.

branches.effect: return it; else sort, cache and return

units.does: Returns sorted entries filtered by tag ids: excluded if any exclude-tag matches; included if includeTags empty or any include-tag matches.

branches.cond: exclude set non-empty and intersects the entry's tags

branches.effect: keep entry; else keep only when it intersects

flags.text: Only reached through SessionArchive.entries(includingTags:) whose only caller is EmuquTests/ArchiveIntegrityTests.swift:270; no production code filters by tags here.

units.does: Returns sorted entries whose start date lies within [startDate, endDate] inclusive.
Takes the lock and reports whether archive.index holds the id.
Takes the lock and reports whether any entry's start date lies within ±toleranceMinutes (default 30) of the date.

Takes the lock; for an indexed id logs a breadcrumb, removes it from the index with a tombstone + deletion time (dropFromIndex, throws on save failure), then moves its file to Trash/ (falls back to deleting it). Unknown ids are a silent no-op.

flags.text: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says delete() '(1) adds to deletedSessionIds and persists, (2) removes from active index, (3) deletes file'; the code moves the file to Trash/<uuid>.session (kept until expireTrash, 90 days) and only deletes it when the move fails.

units.does: Removes the entry from index, inserts a tombstone, records a deletion time, then saves deleted.json then index.json; on any save failure re-appends the entry, removes the tombstone and deletion time, nils caches, re-saves deleted.json (attempt) and rethrows.

branches.effect: roll back in-memory index/tombstone/deletion time, rewrite deleted.json without the id (error swallowed by attempt), rethrow

units.does: Takes the lock; true when the id is in deletedSessionIds.
Takes the lock and returns a copy of deletedSessionIds.
Takes the lock; removes the tombstone, forgets the deletion time and saves deleted.json (throws). Used for trash restore and cross-device restore adoption.
Takes the lock; removes the tombstone, forgets the deletion time and saves deleted.json (throws). Body identical to unmarkAsDeleted.

flags.text: forgetDeletedSession has exactly the same body as unmarkAsDeleted; two names for one operation.

units.does: Takes the lock; inserts a tombstone for the id (need not be archived), records its deletion time and saves deleted.json (throws).
Reads this device's recorded deletion time for the id from UserDefaults archive.deletionTimes (epoch seconds → Date), nil when none.

flags.text: recordDeletionTime writes asynchronously on deletionTimesQueue, and deletionTime reads UserDefaults directly without syncing on that queue; a read right after delete/markAsDeleted can see nil, which CloudKit deletion handling treats as an undated deletion that loses to any restore.

units.does: Returns every UUID that has a recorded deletion time; used to rebuild the tombstone set when deleted.json is unreadable.
Captures now and asynchronously (serial queue, outside archiveLock) sets times[id] = epoch seconds in UserDefaults archive.deletionTimes.
Asynchronously removes the id from the UserDefaults archive.deletionTimes dictionary.
Takes the lock; true when any entry's start date is within SessionArchive.Tuning.importDuplicateWindow (3600 s, exclusive) of the date. Import-time duplicate check.

Takes the lock and archives a batch: each session goes through archiveOne (skip tombstoned/known/in-batch copies, merge into an existing copy/same-sleep entry, or write a new pretty-printed file); new entries are appended and the index saved once; posts per-id change notifications for merged sessions and one nil change notification. Returns new + updated count. On a mid-batch throw, indexes files already written and rethrows.

branches.effect: archiveOne; a throw jumps to catch
indexPartialBatch(newEntries) then rethrow; notifications are not posted
append and saveIndex (throws; files stay written, in-memory index already appended); else skip save

units.does: Appends already-written batch entries to the index and tries to save it (error logged/swallowed by attempt).

One batch item: returns early for a tombstoned id or an already-indexed id; merges into an archived copy/same-sleep target when mergeTarget finds one; skips a copy of a recording written earlier in the batch; otherwise writes it and appends the new entry.

branches.cond: an entry written earlier in this batch overlaps with same type (isCopy)

flags.text: The doc says the batch uses _archive's merge decision including same-sleep overnight segments, but mergeTarget only searches archive.index; two same-sleep segments that both arrive in one batch are not merged (the in-batch check isCopy only catches overlapping copies), so both are written standalone where _archive would fold the second into the first.

units.does: Loads the existing target session, merges the incoming data into it via SessionMerger; when anything changed re-archives the existing session (_archive saves the index itself) and records its id as updated. Any error is logged and the incoming session is dropped.

branches.effect: log and swallow; incoming session dropped and archiveBatch still succeeds

flags.text: A read/write failure on the merge target is logged at .info and swallowed: the imported session is neither written nor counted, archiveBatch returns success, and the import UI only sees a lower count with no error for the lost item.

units.does: Encodes the session with SessionArchive.indexEncoder (prettyPrinted+sortedKeys), encrypting when possible, writes <uuid>.json with format-dependent protection (ledger updated), and returns an entry built by SessionArchiveEntry.make with the bytes-as-written hash.
Posts .flowRecoveryArchiveChanged with object=id for each merged session, then one with object=nil when anything was added or merged.

branches.effect: post the batch-level nil notification; else nothing

units.does: File-private: SHA256-hex of the raw stored bytes compared to entry.fileHash; logs details and throws hashMismatch on mismatch.

branches.effect: return; else log expected/actual/size and throw ArchiveError.hashMismatch
